items.text: to support the warrant article
items.quote: d. mcquaid, motion to support the warrant article, second, m. allison, discussion ensued. n. lockwood had no problem with the article going for town vote, but felt there were pluses and minuses to both sides. k. chenis noted interested parties were in attendance at the last meeting stating they had challenges with selling the property due to the current commercial zoning restricting a dual use of the property. n. lockwood opined that limited business zoning is "messier and less by -right" than commercial zoning. he also noted points previously raised by both the board of selectmen and the property owner noting hardship. roll call vote - m. allison, aye; k. chenis, aye; d. mcquaid, aye; n. lockwood, abstain.

rule.text: An article gets its own thread when it came up at 3 or more meetings, across at least 2 boards, beyond the routine stops every article gets (the Select Board and the Finance Committee each take it up about 2 times to place it and recommend it); when residents spoke about it or a dispute about it was recorded; or when Town Meeting took up an amendment, postponed it, or divided on it, with at least 15 in 100 on the losing side. Those thresholds are our choice, not the town's.

rule.text: An article gets its own thread when it came up at 3 or more meetings, across at least 2 boards, beyond the routine stops every article gets (the Select Board and the Finance Committee each take it up about 2 times to place it and recommend it); when residents spoke about it or a dispute about it was recorded; or when Town Meeting took up an amendment, postponed it, or divided on it, with at least 15 in 100 on the losing side. Those thresholds are our choice, not the town's.

rule.text: An article gets its own thread when it came up at 3 or more meetings, across at least 2 boards, beyond the routine stops every article gets (the Select Board and the Finance Committee each take it up about 2 times to place it and recommend it); when residents spoke about it or a dispute about it was recorded; or when Town Meeting took up an amendment, postponed it, or divided on it, with at least 15 in 100 on the losing side. Those thresholds are our choice, not the town's.

rule.text: An article gets its own thread when it came up at 3 or more meetings, across at least 2 boards, beyond the routine stops every article gets (the Select Board and the Finance Committee each take it up about 2 times to place it and recommend it); when residents spoke about it or a dispute about it was recorded; or when Town Meeting took up an amendment, postponed it, or divided on it, with at least 15 in 100 on the losing side. Those thresholds are our choice, not the town's.

rule.text: An article gets its own thread when it came up at 3 or more meetings, across at least 2 boards, beyond the routine stops every article gets (the Select Board and the Finance Committee each take it up about 2 times to place it and recommend it); when residents spoke about it or a dispute about it was recorded; or when Town Meeting took up an amendment, postponed it, or divided on it, with at least 15 in 100 on the losing side. Those thresholds are our choice, not the town's.

rule.text: An article gets its own thread when it came up at 3 or more meetings, across at least 2 boards, beyond the routine stops every article gets (the Select Board and the Finance Committee each take it up about 2 times to place it and recommend it); when residents spoke about it or a dispute about it was recorded; or when Town Meeting took up an amendment, postponed it, or divided on it, with at least 15 in 100 on the losing side. Those thresholds are our choice, not the town's.
